premises.text: The conditions today are similar to past revolutions that made personal computers accessible.
premises.evidence_span: the conditions today, economical and technological, are very similar to different revolutions that moved us from this computer's large, expensive, difficult to use, to this computer's personal and in every home.

premises.text: Advances in miniaturization and smartphone robotics make home robots more affordable.
premises.evidence_span: the trends that are similar are not only miniaturization and advances in rapid manufacturing and commercialization and manufacturing, reduction of costs of components, but mostly smartphone robotics and cloud robotics.

premises.text: Cloud robotics allows robots to be dynamically upgradable and more affordable.
premises.evidence_span: cloud robotics that takes a computation from the robot into devices you already have, make it much more affordable, and also automatically and dynamically upgradable.

premises.text: Targeted robots for specific tasks can be more affordable and practical for homes.
premises.evidence_span: we're going to have a set of robots that are much more targeted at limited set of tasks that can slowly get into the house because they're more affordable.

premises.text: The Shimmy robot uses smartphone technology to enhance its functionality.
premises.evidence_span: Shimmy is a robotic speaker dog that doesn't just play the music for you. It actually listens to it and enjoys it as much as you do.

premises.text: The robot can perform tasks using cloud-based information for real-time interaction.
premises.evidence_span: it's taking information from the cloud that has the beats, the segments, where the chorus starts, where the verse starts, what genre of the song is.

value.text: Personal robotics can become engaging, affordable, and fun to use in homes.
value.evidence_span: we're going to take this kind of robots, large, expensive, very difficult to use, and move them into engaging, affordable and fun-to-use robots in the home.

notes: Demo issues and Kickstarter details excluded as traction.
